note: Integration record for the Phase 1-6 merge into main, and the baseline identities P7-00 must use.

merge.strategy: git merge --no-ff, no squash and no rebase
merge.why: the dossiers under reports/perf/qjs-align reference specific commit SHAs as baseline, P0/P1 and binary-provenance anchors; rewriting commit identity would strand those references

conflicts_resolved.resolution: kept the phase branch's dossier-only comptime gate and main's `new_target` argument; the sibling simple_ctor_bypass_enabled site auto-merged into exactly this shape, which is what validated the choice

conflicts_resolved.kind: semantic, not textual - the merge compiled cleanly only after a name fix
conflicts_resolved.detail: main renamed the phase branch's `forwarded_leaf` TeardownFlags bit to `special_return` at the same bit position and widened it from Function.call's forwarded leaf to that plus a synchronous native fence. The phase branch's P3-12 ordinary-return classifier still named the old bit, so the build failed; it now lists `special_return`, and the comptime exhaustiveness check re-validates that every bit is classified.
conflicts_resolved.why_safe: both names describe returns that must leave the ordinary .next resume path, so the classification is unchanged and the wider meaning only makes including it more correct

conflicts_resolved.kind: parallel rewrite of the same harness
conflicts_resolved.phase_change: +1328/-54, adding the provenance, validation and ABBA machinery the campaign's exit line depends on
conflicts_resolved.resolution: took the phase branch version wholesale, because every Phase 0-6 artifact including the frozen baseline was produced by it
conflicts_resolved.DROPPED: main's session support (BENCH_SESSIONS / benchInterleaved) is dropped by this resolution and needs a follow-up to re-land on top; it was not blended silently

perf_self_check.note: compares against the checked-in zjs self baseline

same_runtime_p0_sentinel.reading: within noise of the Phase 6 snapshot; the exit line still passes

p7_00_baseline_identities.note: the merge tree's source differs from c95e574d only by the three conflict resolutions plus a zig fmt pass, so the existing Phase 6 snapshot remains usable as global background. P7-00 still needs to collect its own zero-change allocator baseline.

incidents.what: zig fmt --check was never run during the BigInt work
incidents.detail: src/tests/core.zig was not fmt-clean on the phase branch; the appended BigInt tests had unaligned array literals. Fixed in the merge. Cosmetic, but it is a repository gate that the per-cut discipline should have included and did not.

incidents.what: a pre-existing stash was dropped and recovered
incidents.detail: while redoing the merge I stashed a conflicted tree, switched branches, popped it, and then ran `git stash drop`, which removed the pre-existing `wip/generalized-canonical-pmu-driver` stash rather than my own. It was recovered from the dangling commit c3072b2d via `git stash store` and verified: three parents intact, including the six untracked files (pmu_driver.py, instrument_policy.json, the driver test and the 1a workloads).

incidents.what: the first merge attempt was abandoned
incidents.detail: switching branches mid-conflict destroyed MERGE_HEAD, so the merge was reset and redone from main without leaving the branch. Nothing was committed from the first attempt.
